title: Life as an Age and the Covering of the Face
english: The Greek word is an evangelical word. For this reason, therefore, this parable was spoken: 'for a parable' thus 'us as a nation among the nations'. If anyone wishes to interpret the captives, they use us, saying: 'Behold, these ones having been led away well before... God, when the right hand of God and the light of his face were protecting them, they fell into a most evil leading away' (Ps 78:49). If anyone therefore wishes to show a falling away, they refer to us. And 'made us a parable' is not in [Israel], not in Israel, not in the Hebrew multitude, but 'among the nations'.

Those who are truly nations do not know the difference between good and evil, but they consider all pleasant things and all appropriate things to be good, and the opposites of these to be evil. And the name of the parable may be this: the rank of the saints has a certain superiority compared to the other ranks of men. Because of this, they have become a parable. See: men are often taken captive in different ways by enemies. One suffers the taking away of what he has possessed, while another has them remaining... in the winter and the storm of this life, they have their own... flows away into corruption. 15 A head-movement among the peoples. ... they observe [those] changing from prosperity into adversity, to move... those or perhaps grieving. 224 But a head-movement among the peoples we have become. 'Peoples' indeed all the coarsest men can be called, having nothing opened, not being afraid. These therefore, because of us, set a head-movement. We, having become toward the peoples, the coarsest men, moved their mind and their head. And the mind moves when... when it perceives the things being imposed upon it to be perceived. 16 All the day my trouble is against me.

It is. He says 'all the day' and 'through life'. A man's life is called that which is from birth until death, sometimes called one day, sometimes an age. Thus it is said: 'I will not eat meat for ever' (Gen 9:4), and: 'he shall be thy servant for ever' (Ps 18:25). I had trouble against me all this day which I endured for the sake of others (Ps 34:5); and the shame of my face covered me. The shame of the inner man covered me. For my face was not destroyed, but it was covered. And it is possible, having cast off the single covering, to bear his face naked, illuminated, as it is according to nature. And, so that I may phrase it this way, the ignorance that happens to other men destroys their face; for others become from others, from men serpents and wolves and foxes. But the holy man, even if he does not bear his own face naked, has it covered. And it is covered by the arrangement of the body, becoming a seeming ignorance from the incarnation. But when a change occurs into quality, I do not say that the fox, like Herod, had a covering, but his nature and disposition were such. When someone becomes foolish among the thoughtless, having cast folly upon himself, he has his face covered; when he becomes lawless among the lawless, he has his face covered.

From a voice reproaching and speaking idly. He says this: those are reproaching me and speaking idly. And those speaking idly are straying. So he says this: those who oppose us... as the rational [being] is accustomed to have, but rather they are straying. To speak idly is to say superfluous things.
